messages:
Sam K: Hey team — customer reported intermittent 403s after we rotated their service key yesterday. They see it only when they include an X-Project header (x-redwood-project) along with the org header. Sample failure: 

Response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"unauthorized"}
x-redwood-request-id: req_8f3a2c9b

Happens ~10% of requests from their app. Time window: 2026-03-15 14:05–14:20 UTC. Can we triage? They provided one curl but it's missing verbose headers.

Maria S: Thanks Sam. Can you ask them for a curl with -v that includes both headers and the Authorization? Also need the exact request-id for each failure. Example repro curl to ask them to run:

```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <SERVICE_KEY>" \
  -H "x-redwood-org: org_abc123" \
  -H "x-redwood-project: proj_customer" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

Tell them to paste the full curl stdout/stderr including response headers (we need x-redwood-request-id). Also ask them to try removing the project header to confirm the pattern. :mag:

Sam K: Posted that to the customer. They returned one verbose trace: includes request id req_8f3a2c9b and this debug snippet: 

"recv: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 47
X-Redwood-Request-Id: req_8f3a2c9b

{"error":"forbidden: org/project mismatch"}"

Alex R: Hmm — "org/project mismatch" implies the token's org scope doesn't include the project or the request header canonicalization is swapping headers somewhere (proxy). Two quick checks: 
- Confirm the key in use belongs to org_abc123 and that proj_customer is under that org (customer might have created a proj in different org by accident).
- Ask them for the token info payload (we can reconstruct from the token id) or give us the service key id (masked).

Also from infra side, please ask them to run this against our staging edge to rule out upstream proxies: 

```bash
REDWOOD_API_URL=https://staging-api.redwood.ai \ncurl -v -X POST $REDWOOD_API_URL/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <SERVICE_KEY>" \
  -H "x-redwood-org: org_abc123" \
  -H "x-redwood-project: proj_customer" \
  -d '{"input":"ping"}'
```

Maria S: They gave the (masked) key id: sk_live_********123. They confirmed proj_customer is visible in their org UI under a different org id (org_def456) — likely their client-side config is flipping headers on certain requests. They also attached a browser console stack showing a fetch that rewrites headers via middleware.

Support-bot: Note: Key sk_live_********123 belongs to org_org_abc123 per internal mapping. Last rotation event: deploy-bot rotated keys at 2026-03-15T13:50:12Z.

Sam K: Given the mismatch, we need a reproducible curl that fails and one that succeeds. Action items for customer: 
1) Run the curl examples above (prod and staging) and paste full -v output.
2) If possible, capture the failing request from their app (HAR or tcpdump) showing the exact headers that reached our edge.
3) Provide the x-redwood-request-id for at least two failures and the corresponding local timestamp for correlation.

Alex R: From our side I'll grep edge logs for the request ids and time range: 

```bash
sudo journalctl -u redwood-edge --since "2026-03-15 14:00" --until "2026-03-15 14:30" | rg "req_8f3a|sk_live_\*\*\*123|org_abc123|proj_customer" -n
```

If we see header canonicalization or there's a mismatch between the auth claim's org and the x-redwood-org header we'll know. Also check gateway for duplicate header compression settings.

Maria S: Customer sent two more req ids: req_8f3a2c9b (403) and req_b12f4a01 (200 when they removed x-redwood-project). They also uploaded a HAR to our debug-bundle endpoint and granted access. Link: https://debug.redwood.ai/bundles/BUCKET/xyz (internal only).

Alex R: I'm pulling logs now. Quick theory: a client-side proxy rewrites the project header to a project in a different org for a subset of traffic (A/B middleware). That would explain intermittent rate. If logs show auth claim org != x-redwood-org, we should return a clearer error message indicating the mismatch with the request-id to help customers fix it.

Sam K: Agreed — if we can reproduce locally against staging that seals it. Maria, can you ask the customer to run a quick diagnostic that prints token introspection? If they can't share the secret, we can ask for the token id and we'll introspect. Example command for them (non-secret): 

```bash
# return token meta (runs on our side if they share id)
# or they can paste the Authorization header value (masked)
```

Maria S: Got it. I'll request token id and the two -v curl outputs, plus permission to pull the debug bundle. Also asked them to confirm whether any CDN or edge workers may rewrite headers. :pray:

Support-bot: Ticket #INC-2026-331 created for this escalation. Assigned to Alex R and Sam K.

Alex R: I'll follow up with findings in this thread once I finish correlating logs. If we confirm header flipping, ops can roll a temporary check that rejects mismatched combos with clearer reason.

Sam K: Thanks everyone. I'll keep the customer updated and paste their verbose outputs here when I get them. :thumbsup:
